parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and is phrased as an obligation ('We need to show'), never as a proven fact. The text's only all-n argument is the parity/invariance computation, which explicitly assumes Xiang splits each 2d piece exactly once (t_i=1 for all i, small piece d untouched). Other distributions (cuts bunched in one interval, or cuts placed in the small d piece) are dismissed with 'Need to prove...' and n=2 numerical tests — assertions, not proofs. Nothing elsewhere in the text closes this gap. It is genuinely load-bearing and actually false: for n=2, Liu's 0.4/0.4/0.2 division vs. Xiang cuts at 0.75 and 0.9 gives pieces 0.4, 0.35, 0.1, 0.1, 0.05, so Liu gets 0.4+0.1+0.05 = 0.55 < (n+1)d = 0.6. Thus the lower-bound obligation is unmet (and the targeted value is wrong anyway).
